title: I spent 8 months and $40K+ developing an AI trading platform: quant research, backtesting, live strategy automation, indicators, and more
author: person-person12
selftext:
In my experience as a trader, almost every AI tool, site, and piece of software in this space only does **one thing** in my workflow. I kept running into the same issues, asking **the exact same exact question as thousands of other traders…**  
  
*"Why am I paying for a* ***dozen*** *different tools for a* ***dozen*** *different things?"*  
  
**-----**  
  
The answer I wanted was [one platform that does all of it, for a fraction of the cost;](https://www.wealthlearn.ca)  


i) An **AI-powered hub** that **researches**, **backtests**, and **automates** **strategies** **live** (*or to TopStep*) across **10,000+ instruments** and with **10+ years** of multi-timeframe history included, *no coding experience or data required.*

ii) An **AI mode**l that builds any **custom TradingView indicator** in *Pine Script v6.*

iii) Professionally built **indicators** for popular concepts: ***OTE/STDV, Bookmap-style order flow*** *proxies for TradingView,* and ***Volume Profile (****AMT****).***

iv) *Real-time* **news**, intraday **GEX** levels, sector overviews, and **order flow** feeds.

v) Advanced **stock screening**: *earnings, key metrics, fundamentals, analyst opinions, TradingView charting, and live news.*

vi) **Daily**, **weekly**, and **monthly** pre-market **AI stock picks**, performance-tracked, built from thousands of factors in a custom database.

vii) A **100% free**, start-to-finish, beginner-to-expert course packed with structured learning paths, interactive lessons + exercises, and a full glossary, *that I wish I had when I first started.*

viii) **Dedicated local-execution software** for **TopStep** that abides by their API rules and includes custom charting, economic calendars, volume standard-deviation gauges, and more.

ix) a hub to connect to a **live brokerage**, analyze positions, model long-term portfolios, and monitor my algorithms.  

# And most importantly, ONE AI agent that can actually do all of it.

**-----**  
  
Because nothing like this existed, I spent eight months relentlessly researching and developing my platform (with the help of the best professional developers I know) to make my dream a reality.  
  
[WealthLearn.ca](http://WealthLearn.ca) brings every feature above into a single platform for a fraction of the cost, so you can stop tangling together scattered tools and paying for a dozen separate subscriptions.   
  
It connects directly with **TradingView**, **live brokerages** (*Wealthsimple, Moomoo, Kraken, Coinbase, Webull, and more)*, and TopStep... **having two clear goals;**  


**1) Bring the benefits of quant** and **algo trading** to **retail traders,** **WITHOUT** the coding, complexity, or the institutional price tag.

2) **Unify every tool needed, from day trading to macro investing, into one ecosystem,** instead of a dozen expensive, single-purpose tools.  

**--**  
  
Happy to answer anything and everything in the comments. I really don't want this to feel like a pitch, but there's so much low-effort vibe-coded stuff going around right now that I thought something I've poured this much real work into could actually be useful to people. Feel free to watch the video attached for a glimpse of what we've built, and if you don't want to spend anything, there's a free trial so you can see exactly what I'm talking about.  


>Educational software and tools, not financial advice.

comments.author: Boonzies
comments.body: So a wrapper powered by Opus 4.8 (Anthropic Claude) and AI assistants like QuantCodeGPT for writing backtest rules and PineDesign GPT for generating TradingView Pine Script v6 indicators...nice. But the AI is only the LLM that writes the scripts, I don't see how it helps design the scripts. Writing and designing are two different beasts. How does your software assure good scripting without backtesting an overfit model.

I had to code a json schema "I do have a pinescript to json" translator though

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
You could not be more wrong. I honestly dont know what product you think you're describing here, so I'm going to break it down piece by piece.

**First, calling WealthLearn a “wrapper” is just factually wrong.**

Claude is one reasoning layer used by the product but it isn't the product. it doesn't prepare the market data, run the candles, track strategy state, calculate fills, apply costs, build trade logs, calculate the analytics, connect to the user's account, or enforce live execution. **Our own systems do that.**

The current **AlgoAgent beta** only released around a month ago. Users can operate the site directly, or let the Agent call the same tools.

Second, **QuantCodeGPT** doesn't just “help write backtest rules.”

QuantCodeGPT is our legacy backtesting and automation model being originally built around TopstepX strategy automation. It takes the user's instructions or source material, identifies missing requirements, turns the completed idea into an executable strategy package, validates it, runs the backtest, and lets the user upload the tested strategy file into DelDirect for local execution.

PineDesignGPT is a separate product, and if you had actually used then this would've been obvious.

The user starts on WealthLearn with a description , existing Pine source, PDF, or YouTube transcript. The site stores that request & creates a short-lived one-time handoff code, then it copies it when PineDesignGPT opens.

The GPT redeems the code and receives the prompt, requested output type, and source text tied to that session. It reads the rules, works out the Pine structure, fills in missing implementation details, and produces the entire Pine v6 file. It has a required validation checklist, writes the full script to a downloadable .pine file, then sends the complete source, file name, line count, status and diagnostics back into WealthLearn. The site gives it a return link and checks for the completed file every few seconds, then shows the result with copy and download controls.

*That custom GPT setup existed because before we could afford to carry every model and runtime cost ourselves, we used the runtime already available through the user's own ChatGPT account. It was a cost decision but wasn't the product.*

Now for the AlgoAgent, because this is where your description gets **even further away from reality.**

The Agent has a real tool-use loop. It reads the request, picks a WealthLearn tool, calls it and receives the actual output. It doesn't just write a paragraph pretending it performed an action like many "wrappers."

It can run research and custom studies, build and save strategies, run Monte Carlo and prop-firm simulations, grade holdings, screen stocks, build Pine indicators, read market data and GEX, inspect the user's strategies and backtests, read a connected brokerage account, and prepare an order for confirmation from user.

The Agent doesn't secretly place or arm live trades on its own. It can prepare the order and the user confirms it. Same with deployment, sizing and account selection. Those stay under the user's control.

And here is the main part you completely missed: **the model is not the backtest runner.**

The model's job is to understand the request and produce a structured executable package. The runner is what actually does the test.

The package contains a strategy.js file with a fixed contract. createStrategy() has to return init() and onBar(). init() sets the strategy up. onBar() runs once for every candle (in time order) and holds persistent state inside the strategy itself

Before the package is accepted its checked against the package contract, scanned for banned code and unsafe access, checked for lookahead, and passed through a sandbox validator. Rule-based fixes run first. If it still fails, the generator can repair and validate it again, with a capped repair loop. A package that still fails isn't quietly passed through as if it worked.

**Then the actual runner takes over.**

There are different data lanes depending on the job. An in-chat AlgoAgent study on a US stock or ETF pulls the user's Alpaca historical bars in the browser after they click Run Study. The main local backtesting runner can also work from versioned, compressed historical market-data segments prepared by WealthLearn.

That runner checks the device cache, finds the missing segments, downloads only what it needs, retries failures, verifies hashes, decompresses the files, parses them into candles, filters the dates, and puts the bars in market order.

**Only after the candles are built does strategy execution begin.**

The JavaScript package is loaded and createStrategy() is called & the runner refuses it if init() and onBar() arent there. It starts with the requested capital, quantity, symbol and timeframe, then walks every candle one by one.  It only sees the candles up to the current index, which stops it from reading tomorrow's bar aka. look ahead.

Entries use an actual fill model as the normal path queues a signal on one candle and fills it at the next candle's open and a signal on the final candle is dropped because there is no executable next-bar fill. Open positions are checked candle by candle for stops and targets, with the stop checked before the target on the same bar.

The runner tracks long or short direction, size, entry and exit time, holding period, stop, target, gross and net PnL, commissions, slippage, point value, tick size, tick value, favorable excursion, adverse excursion, planned risk-reward and realized R multiple. It handles futures pricing through instrument specs instead of pretending every contract is one share of stock.

While it runs it reports real progress, yields so the page doesn't freeze, supports cancellation, and has a silence limit so broken code can't sit there forever.

**Once execution is finished, the result isn't just “30% win rate.”**

It builds the trade list and equity curve, then calculates total return, max drawdown, Sharpe ratio, profit factor, daily returns and a buy-and-hold comparison. It classifies bars into regimes, tags trades by regime, produces regime and period breakdowns, then builds the final result used by the rest of the product.

**That is the backtest runner you somehow reduced to** ***“the LLM writes a script.”***

The live side is separate again. Live strategy code runs in a locked execution context with no fetch, imports, process access, timers or outside access. It replays the full closed-bar history to rebuild the strategy's state, then only returns the signal from the newest closed candle.

Even then, the signal isn't blindly sent to a broker. The server treats it as an untrusted request, checks it against the saved deployment, live settings, broker support and order rules, and uses an idempotency key so the same signal can't create the same order twice.

So the backtest runner, study runner, live runner and order relay are separate pieces. Claude is not sitting there pretending to be all four.

**QuantCodeGPT** can also hand a completed strategy into DelDirect, a separate Electron desktop app for futures execution through ProjectX and Topstep-connected firms.

**DelDirect** has its own strategy importer, schema checks, bar aggregation, live and risk engines, paper order lifecycle, local credential storage, device binding, charting, economic calendar and performance analytics. That includes equity, daily PnL, trade logs, time-window breakdowns, expectancy, drawdown, profit factor and win/loss diagnostics.

The execution engine runs on the user's machine. Of course it still calls broker and market-data services because it's trading software. The WealthLearn account and device check is the access gate, not the trading engine itself.

**And those are only a few parts of the site.**

*We also run GEX levels, TradingView GEX overlays, real-time headlines, earnings, company metrics, stock screening, portfolio construction, holdings analysis, saved strategy monitoring and broader investment research.*

**So no , this is not “an LLM that writes scripts.”**

The model interprets the request and chooses which WealthLearn tools to call but the actual work is done by the data services, validators, study engine, backtest runner, analytics engine, live runtime, order gate, desktop software and broker connections.

**What it won't do is magically hand every user a profitable strategy.**

It helps the user research an idea, define it, measure it, reject bad ideas, improve better ones, and automate trading strategies that survive their own testing.

**So your 30% point doesn't prove the software failed. It proves the strategy you tested failed.**

**That is literally why the backtest exists**.  
  
A real testing tool is supposed to give you an ugly answer when the rules have no edge. It isn't supposed to change the result until you feel good about it.

And saying you built a “bulletproof 65%+ win rate strategy” doesn't fix the argument either as a win rate on its own says almost nothing. A strategy can win 65% of the time and still lose money if its losses are much larger than its wins. It can also look incredible historically because somebody kept changing rules until the same old data finally looked good (overfitting) .

**The product helps you test an edge. It doesn't manufacture one because you asked nicely.**

*I didn't want to make a long message to come across as disrespectful, but considering the amount of efforts that our team has put into our products, I did not want to let a major oversimplification go without correction.*

comments.body: Basically a sub par scalarfield.io clone

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
|Capability|Composer|ScalarField|WealthLearn|
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|AI / no-code strategy building|Yes|Yes|Yes|
|Backtesting|Yes|Yes (multi-dataset)|Yes|
|Automated live execution|Yes full auto-rebalance|Yes|Yes|
|Brokerage model|Own broker-dealer|Connect broker|Connect your own broker|
|Stocks / ETFs|Yes|Yes|Yes|
|Options|Some|Yes|No|
|Crypto|No|Not stated|Yes|
|Futures + prop firm execution|No|No|Yes (local desktop)|
|Prediction markets / pre-IPO|No|Yes|No|
|TradingView-native Pine v6 builder|No|No|Yes|
|Prebuilt indicators (OTE/STDV, VP, flow)|No|No|Yes|
|Intraday GEX levels / order flow context|No|Not its focus|Yes|
|Stock / option screening|In-builder|Yes|Yes (stocks)|
|Insider / senator data|No|Yes|No|
|Community strategies / templates|3,000+|Yes|No|
|Full free education course|No|No|Yes|
|Built for|Passive systematic ETF/stock investors|Quant / power users|Active no-code retail traders|

  
TLDR: **Composer** is for hands-off automated investing in stocks and ETFs, **Scalar Field** is for AI-driven research and portfolio automation & **WealthLearn** is for no-code retail traders who want the entire quant and algo workflow in one place.

**Composer** is significantly larger than **Scalar Field,** and **Scalar Field** is significantly bigger than **WealthLearn**. That's just how funding and time in the market tend to work which makes sense given thats their founding order too.

Three platforms, same broad space, three different traders. That isn't cloning, **that's a category.** Happy to go deeper on any row if you actually want to compare them properly.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
Oh it definitely will. AI companies took over 80% of funding in Q1 this year w/ roughly **$242 billion** poured into an already crowded space, but surprisingly not as much finance-related innovation compared to other industries IMO.

That said, I could name countless other products similar to the ones above, and all of them have room to grow, especially given the legal constraints around a lot of this stuff. A lot of sites are bound to the borders of the jurisdiction they operate out of, so theres real global opportunity on top of a steadily growing space. 

It’s funny bc having competition also raises the value of your own company when it inflates your sector (cough, cough, AI bubble mega-caps).

Thanks for the reply.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: We run a few thousand calls a day, pulled in on a schedule in batches and served off our own database, so it stays steady whether it’s a 100 people or 10k on the site. We batch a few hundred names into one call so the number scales with how much we cover and how often we refresh, not with how many users are on it. They all serve their own respective purposes and ingestions obv

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
Honestly it wasnt one cheque.   
  
It was eight months of full time work and a stack of costs that add up quick when youre building this many things at once. The biggest piece was the build itself, the time, plus the developers I brought in on the heavier parts as I wasnt about to be the only person touching code that can move someones money.   
  
Then legal / compliance which becomes its own monster the second your software can connect to a real brokerage and fire a real order, so a serious chunk went there before I ever let a user near live execution. Security sits on top of that.   
  
Then the data, as good market data costs real money and never stops, youre paying every single day to keep quotes, fundamentals, news and years of history fresh across thousands of instruments instead of scraping free junk that falls apart.  
  
The AI runs up a bill of its own, as the agent and the build tools sit on a serious model and our own runtime and we carry that ourselves so the user isnt paying per call. And under all of it is the infrastructure running 24/7, the storage, the background jobs keeping everything fresh, and the hundred smaller things nobody thinks about like the domain, design and the tooling it takes to actually run a site this size.   
  
So no, that number isnt a flex. Its just what it takes to build something this wide and this real in under a year instead of one tool with a nice landing page. A good portion of these costs were one-time expenses and are not reoccurring, but were a necessity to building out our vision
